title: Igneous Rocks
text: Igneous rocks form when molten magma or lava cools and solidifies.

title: Stratigraphic Superposition
text: In an undisturbed sequence of sedimentary rock layers, lower layers are older than the layers above them.

title: Metamorphic Rocks
text: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are changed by heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids without completely melting.

title: Xylem
text: Xylem tissue transports water and dissolved minerals from roots toward the rest of a plant.

title: Stomata
text: Stomata are pores in plant surfaces that allow gas exchange and water vapor loss; guard cells regulate their opening.

title: Phloem
text: Phloem transports sugars and other organic products from sources, such as mature leaves, to sinks where they are used or stored.

title: Phonemes
text: A phoneme is a sound category that can distinguish one word from another in a language.

title: Morphemes
text: A morpheme is the smallest unit in a language that carries meaning or grammatical function.

title: Syntax
text: Syntax is the set of rules that governs how words combine into phrases and sentences.

title: Domain Name System
text: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses used to locate internet services.

title: Transmission Control Protocol
text: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) provides a reliable, ordered byte stream between endpoints, retransmitting lost data when needed.

title: Internet Protocol
text: Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and routes packets across networks using a best-effort service that does not guarantee delivery or ordering.
